newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU monetary committee meets on EMU budget pact.
newsitem.headline: EU monetary committee meets on EMU budget pact.

text.p: The European Union's monetary committee began a meeting on Wednesday to resolve differences over a budget stability pact for countries joining a common currency.

The meeting of national treasury and central bank officials comes amid continued disagreement over details of the budget disciplinary accord which seeks to keep budget deficits under three percent of total output.
In particular, there is no agreement on a definition of the economic circumstances which would let a government inside monetary union avoid sanctions.

Germany wants an economic downturn defined numerically while others, in particular France, say it would be preferrable to have a more flexible approach that takes account of the economic differences within EU countries.

EU monetary sources said they did not expect the monetary committee to resolve the dispute and predicted the group would simply lay out the options for EU finance ministers who meet in Dublin on Thursday.
"I expect (agreement) will have to wait until the ministers meet," said one source familiar with the committee's delilberations.
Sources said the ministers are expected to focus on two options: a single figure that specifies the magnitude of a economic recession and a range, or box.

"I think the direction in which we are moving is a hard figure on the one hand and a kind of box," said one EU official, adding the range of figures for the latter could be between zero and negative two percent.
The parameters of the box are still open for discussion and it is unclear whether Germany is willing to accept this approach, officials added.
The challenge is to make such an option watertight and allay German fears that it would not be another loophole for governments to avoid sanctions.
Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet said on Wednesday he had "no doubt" EU countries would iron out their differences and agree a stability pact.
